text: Acme-corp's platform team keeps hearing the same complaint: every new service starts as a copy-pasted repo, with CI config that's slightly stale and no entry in the catalog until someone notices weeks later. This lab builds the real fix -- one golden-path template that produces a brand-new service with its pipeline, its monitoring dashboard, and its catalog entry already correct on day one.

The template's form stays deliberately small -- just a service name and an owning team, both required. A golden path earns its name by making the easy path the correct one, and every value a developer doesn't have to type by hand is a value that can't be typed wrong. Everything else the new service needs gets filled in automatically from those two fields.

The skeleton underneath the form is where golden path stops being a slogan. Its CI config doesn't define build, test, scan, and deploy from scratch -- it extends Chapter 6's shared pipeline template, so a fix to that template reaches this new service the same way it reaches every other one. Its catalog-info.yaml ships pre-filled with the owner and service name, instead of waiting for someone to add it after the fact.

Four scaffolder actions run in order to make this real. fetch:template fills the skeleton's placeholders with the form's values. publish:github pushes that filled-in skeleton as an actual GitHub repository. catalog:register adds the new service to the catalog automatically, closing the loop Chapter 2 opened. And fs:rename seeds empty dev, staging, and prod overlay directories in the GitOps config repo, so the new pipeline has somewhere real to deploy to.

Running the template for a new order-notifications service isn't done when the wizard finishes -- it's done when two separate checks both pass. The CI tool has to show build, test, scan, and deploy all green, with ArgoCD syncing it into the dev environment. And the catalog has to resolve the same service by name, with the right owner and lifecycle. Green CI only proves the pipeline ran; a resolving catalog entry proves registration actually worked, and that's the half that fails silently most often.

Lesson 29 built one golden-path template and proved both halves of it work. Lesson 30 picks up where this one leaves off, wiring a GitOps-driven canary rollout for a real app, complete with automated rollback the moment a bad metric shows up.
